n: int; required scalar; number of candidate items N, in items; must satisfy n>=0 and equal the number of entries in items. Item indices start at 0 and end at n-1. When n=0, items must be []; n=1 is valid.
cx: float (JSON number, integer notation allowed); required real scalar; x-coordinate of the centre of the fixed circular container. Length unit unspecified; uses the same unit as cy, R, item side lengths and solution coordinates. Together with cy and R it must satisfy the placeholder-outside-circle condition stated in the R field.
cy: float (JSON number, integer notation allowed); required real scalar; y-coordinate of the centre of the fixed circular container. Length unit unspecified; uses the same unit as cx, R, item side lengths and solution coordinates. Together with cx and R it must satisfy the placeholder-outside-circle condition stated in the R field.
R: float (JSON number, integer notation allowed); required real scalar; radius of the fixed circular container, must be strictly greater than zero, using the same length unit as all geometric coordinates and side lengths. Every valid input must also satisfy (-1-cx)^2+(-1-cy)^2>R^2, so that the fixed placeholder point (-1,-1) lies strictly outside the circle; this must hold even when n=0. Inputs whose placeholder point lies inside the circle or on its circumference are invalid.
items: list[list[float]] (all values are JSON numbers, integer notation allowed); required, shape n×2. The outer index i starts at 0 and corresponds to the i-th item; each inner list must contain exactly two reals strictly greater than zero, in the fixed order [L_i,W_i]. L_i at inner index 0 is the side length along the x-axis when unrotated, and W_i at inner index 1 is the side length along the y-axis when unrotated; length unit unspecified, consistent with R, cx, cy and solution coordinates. After a 90-degree rotation the two axis-aligned side lengths are swapped. [] when n=0. Items that cannot fit into the circle even alone may still be given as candidates; not every item is required to be packable.
rotation_enabled: int; required scalar, no default; may only be 0 or 1, dimensionless, corresponding to the global rotation permission parameter g of the mathematical model. 0 means rotation is forbidden for all items; 1 means each packed item may choose to be unrotated or rotated by 90 degrees. This field is a global input permission, not a per-item rotation decision; r[i] of unpacked items must always be 0. No other rotation angles are allowed.
